content.overview: Section 32 allows a company proposing to make an offer of securities to issue a red herring prospectus prior to the issue of a prospectus. It must be filed with the Registrar at least three days prior to the opening of the subscription list and the offer, carries the obligations of a prospectus, and requires variations between the red herring and the final prospectus to be highlighted. After the offer closes, the final prospectus must state the total capital raised and other prescribed details.
content.glance: Red herring prospectus before the full prospectus; file at least three days before offer opens; same obligations as a prospectus; highlight variations in the final prospectus.
content.study: A red herring prospectus is a prospectus that does not include complete particulars of the quantum or price of the securities. A company proposing an offer of securities may issue a red herring prospectus prior to the issue of a prospectus. It must be filed with the Registrar at least three days before the opening of the subscription list and the offer. Upon closing of the offer of securities, the prospectus stating the total capital raised (whether by way of debt or share capital), the closing price of the securities and other prescribed details must be filed with the Registrar and SEBI. Any variation between the red herring prospectus and the prospectus must be highlighted as variations. The obligations under the Act as are applicable to a prospectus apply to a red herring prospectus. Current-law framing: identify use of a red herring; check the three-day filing rule; apply prospectus obligations; require highlighted variations and post-offer filing.

sections.heading: Meaning and Purpose
sections.body: A red herring prospectus omits complete quantum or price particulars and is used before the final prospectus to test the market.

sections.heading: Filing Before Offer
sections.body: It must be filed with the Registrar at least three days prior to the opening of the subscription list and the offer.

sections.heading: Prospectus Obligations
sections.body: Obligations applicable to a prospectus apply to a red herring prospectus; variations in the final prospectus must be highlighted.

sections.heading: Post-Offer Filing
sections.body: After the offer closes, a prospectus stating total capital raised, closing price and prescribed details must be filed with the Registrar and SEBI.

examples.title: Compliant red herring
examples.body: A company files a red herring prospectus with the ROC at least three days before the offer opens, then files the final prospectus highlighting variations and post-offer capital details.

examples.title: Late filing
examples.body: A red herring is filed only one day before the subscription list opens. Section 32’s three-day rule is breached.

hypotheticals.question: Is a red herring free of prospectus liability?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Obligations applicable to a prospectus apply to a red herring prospectus under s. 32.

hypotheticals.question: Must price be fixed in the red herring?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. By definition it does not include complete particulars of quantum or price; those appear in the final prospectus.

distinctions.title: Red herring (s. 32) vs shelf prospectus (s. 31)
distinctions.left: Pre-final prospectus for a single offer process, without complete price/quantum
distinctions.right: Multi-issue prospectus over a validity period with information memoranda

misconceptions.trap: A red herring is only a marketing document with no legal obligations.
misconceptions.correction: Section 32 applies prospectus obligations to the red herring and requires highlighted variations in the final prospectus.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 32 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify red herring use. II. Check three-day ROC filing. III. Apply prospectus obligations. IV. Check variations and post-offer filing. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Red herring status; filing timeline; obligations; variations; post-offer filing; precise relief.

examTips: Note highlighted variations and post-offer filing.
